overview: Melrose Industries is a UK-listed, pure-play global aerospace and defence business operating as GKN Aerospace, formed after the April 2023 demerger of its Automotive and Powder Metallurgy divisions into Dowlais Group. It designs and manufactures flight-critical engine structures, aerostructures and electrical wiring systems through two divisions, Engines and Airframes, acting as a 'Super-Tier 1' partner to all major engine and airframe OEMs. Melrose operates more than 30 manufacturing sites across 12 countries, with technology embedded on roughly 100,000 flights a day across civil (narrowbody, widebody, business jets) and defence (fixed-wing and rotorcraft) platforms.

business_model.summary: Revenue is generated from engine and airframe structural components sold both as original equipment (OE) to OEMs during the production ramp and as aftermarket parts, repairs and risk-and-revenue-sharing partnership (RRSP) royalties over the life of each programme. Engines content is dominated by RRSPs with engine-makers (Pratt & Whitney, GE Aerospace, Rolls-Royce), which provide decades-long, largely annuity-like aftermarket cash flow once engines enter service; Airframes is a design-to-build partner with high sole-source content on major civil and defence platforms. Civil aerospace and defence represented 71%/29% of H1 2026 Group revenue (FY2025: 71%/29%).

revenue_streams.name: Engines - Aftermarket (incl. RRSP variable consideration, repairs, governmental)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2G - engine OEMs (Pratt & Whitney, GE Aerospace, Rolls-Royce), airframe OEMs (Airbus, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems) and government/defence customers (US DoD, UK MoD, Swedish FMV, NATO members)
business_model.geographic_mix: Global manufacturing footprint across 12 countries (US, UK, Sweden, Netherlands, Mexico, China JV and others); end-customer revenue weighted to North America and Europe with a growing China JV presence via COMAC (C909/C919/C929 programmes)

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest independent (non-OEM-owned) Tier 1/Super-Tier 1 suppliers of engine structures and aerostructures globally, with embedded, often sole-sourced content on essentially all high-volume civil and major defence platforms; GKN Aerospace is RRSP partner on 19 engine families, with six generating ~90% of RRSP portfolio value

moat_factors.description: Risk-and-revenue-sharing partnerships entitle Melrose to decades of aftermarket cash flow (management targets ~$27bn of cash over the life of engine programmes) once OE content is designed onto an engine, with minimal re-competition risk during the programme's life
Over 70% of Airframes content is sole-sourced; positions are typically locked in for the life of the aircraft/engine programme due to high recertification costs and switching costs for OEMs

Proprietary additive manufacturing (e.g., Fan Case Mount Ring on PW1500G, first FAA-certified large-scale additive load-bearing engine structure) differentiates Melrose and is being adopted by Pratt & Whitney, GE Aerospace and Rolls-Royce
Holds military type certificate for RM12 (Gripen C/D) with RM16 (Gripen E) in progress; ~25-year Airbus wing partnership; century-long FMV relationship

moat_factors.factor: Scale and diversification across civil/defence, OE/aftermarket
moat_factors.description: Diversification across four Engines business models (RRSPs, commercial contracts, repair, governmental) reduces single-program concentration risk

weaknesses: Dependent on a small number of large OEM customers (Airbus, Boeing, Pratt & Whitney, GE, Rolls-Royce) for the majority of volume
Airframes margins (6-8%) are structurally far lower than Engines (32-34%), weighing on blended Group margin
Exposed to OEM build-rate volatility and supply chain bottlenecks (forgings, castings, rare-earth powders) largely outside its control
Significant single-site concentration risk, illustrated starkly by the 2026 Garden Grove incident shutting a key F-35/commercial transparencies facility
High factoring/receivables financing (~£387m) and elevated net debt/leverage (1.8x) versus some peers

growth_drivers: Production rate ramp-up across Airbus (A320neo family targeting 70-75/month by end-2027) and Boeing (737MAX, 787) feeding through to OE content growth
Maturing aftermarket annuity from newer-generation engines (GTF, GEnx, XWB) as RRSP variable consideration grows with fleet installed base and shop visits
Structural increase in defence spending - NATO members moving from 2% to a 3.5%-of-GDP pathway by 2035, European ReArm Plan (€800bn by 2029), and proposed US defence budget increases
Expansion into uncrewed/autonomous air vehicles (FMV demonstrator in Sweden, Anduril/Project NYX in UK, BAE Systems Collaborative Combat Aircraft 'Brontanax')
Commercialisation of proprietary additive fabrication technology across both Engines and Airframes, opening new high-margin content opportunities
Positioning on next-generation programmes (CFMI RISE, Pratt & Whitney next-gen GTF, 6th-generation fighters, electric/urban air mobility e.g. Archer Midnight)
Engine parts repair business growth (multi-year contracts with Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney, Boeing) as a high-growth, capital-light aftermarket segment
Management's 2029 medium-term targets: ~£5bn revenue, 24%+ margin, ~£1.2bn+ adjusted operating profit, >20% EPS CAGR, £600m free cash flow

business.description: May 2026 chemical tank incident shut a key GKN transparencies site (F-35 canopies, commercial cabin windows, ~£136m 2025 revenue); site operating at ~50% capacity with full restart targeted for late September 2026, £25-30m of additional H2 exceptional costs, more than 30 civil litigation actions, federal/state regulatory investigations and a $100m claims programme, with total financial impact still not fully quantified

Heavy reliance on a small number of engine OEMs (Pratt & Whitney, GE, Rolls-Royce) and airframe OEMs (Airbus, Boeing) for both OE and aftermarket revenue; loss of content on a major platform would be very difficult to replace

Ongoing shortages/bottlenecks in forgings, castings and rare-earth metal powders constrain Melrose's and its customers' ability to meet OEM build-rate ramps, as repeatedly flagged in FY2025 and H1 2026 results
Pratt & Whitney GTF PW1100G powder metal inspection programme carries an estimated total cash cost to Melrose of ~£200m, with ~£50m expected in 2026 and ongoing PMI payments reducing free cash flow

financial.description: Net debt of £1,530m at H1 2026 (1.8x leverage, within 1.5x-2.0x target range) alongside £387m of non-recourse factoring utilisation; both expected to grow with revenue and are not strictly bank debt but represent real financing reliance

Revenue and costs are substantially USD and EUR-denominated against GBP reporting; FX translation reduced FY2025 revenue/operating profit by £59m/£19m and H1 2026 by £28m/£11m; derivative fair-value swings also create statutory earnings volatility (e.g., statutory operating profit of £154m vs adjusted £347m in H1 2026)
The £175m buyback programme was paused in H1 2026 pending clarity on Garden Grove's financial impact, reducing near-term capital returns

regulatory.description: Federal and California state investigations (including an FBI search warrant), workplace safety inspections and ongoing civil litigation create open-ended liability; criminal charges were not filed by the Orange County DA, but civil enforcement penalties and emergency-service cost claims remain outstanding

US tariffs imposed in 2025 added supply chain cost and complexity before UK/US and EU/US zero-tariff agreements for civil aerospace were reached; future trade policy shifts remain a risk not factored into 2026 guidance
Defence revenue depends on government procurement decisions and export licensing (e.g., Gripen sales to Ukraine/Colombia, UK MoD programmes) which can shift with geopolitics

macro.description: H1 2026 US-Iran conflict disrupted Middle East flight activity and raised jet fuel prices; IATA cut 2026 RPK growth forecast from 4.9% to 2.1%, though impact on Melrose has been limited to date given tight aircraft/engine MRO capacity

While current trend is strongly positive (NATO 3.5% GDP pathway, European rearmament), a future de-escalation or fiscal retrenchment could slow the pace of defence spending growth embedded in guidance upside

Variable-rate bank debt (expected ~5.3% cost of drawn debt for the next 12 months) means higher-for-longer rates raise interest expense; input costs include titanium, composites and energy, partially hedged

execution.description: CFO Matthew Gregory is retiring during 2026 with Ross McCluskey joining as his replacement, introducing near-term leadership transition risk

execution.risk: Execution of production ramp and Brilliant Basics programme
execution.description: Delivering margin expansion and the £600m 2029 FCF target depends on continued execution of the 'Brilliant Basics' lean operating model, inventory reduction (still elevated) and successful capacity investment (Trollhättan, North Charleston, Filton, Mexico) to support OEM rate increases

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Structurally positive: civil aerospace has record order backlogs (Airbus/Boeing backlogs stretching to the 2030s, combined gross orders surging in H1 2026) constrained by OEM build rates, which supports both OE pricing power and a growing engine aftermarket (shop visits, spare parts); defence spending is on a multi-year structural uptrend driven by NATO's 3.5%-of-GDP pathway, European rearmament and rising US defence budgets
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - civil OE demand is linked to the multi-year commercial aircraft cycle and air travel demand, but current record backlogs and supply-constrained build rates are providing a buffer; aftermarket and RRSP annuity revenue is more resilient and counter-cyclical (aging fleets fly longer in downturns); defence revenue is largely non-cyclical, driven by multi-year government budget cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - net debt of ~£1.5bn at a blended cost of drawn debt of ~5.3% means rate moves affect interest expense and FCF; hedging of a portion of interest cost on committed facilities partially mitigates this
key_input_costs: Rare-earth metal powders (used in engine repairs)

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: revenue up 10% to £1,873m, adjusted operating profit up 16% to £347m, margin up 50bps to 18.5%; free cash inflow of £13m, a £67m improvement; interim dividend raised 13% to 2.7p; FY2026 guidance maintained excluding Garden Grove impact

Thermal incident at one of three chemical tanks at GKN Aerospace's Garden Grove, California transparencies facility (key F-35 canopy and commercial cabin window supplier) led to evacuation of ~50,000 residents, temporary site closure, and reduced H1 revenue/operating profit by £16m/£9m
£175m share buyback programme paused pending clarification of the financial, legal and regulatory impact of the Garden Grove incident

Orange County DA closed its criminal investigation into Garden Grove without charges; Melrose announced a claims programme of up to $100m for affected residents/businesses; shares jumped ~8-11% on the news; Kepler Cheuvreux upgraded to Buy

Garden Grove targeted to resume full manufacturing on 28 September 2026 with a phased ramp to full capacity and deliveries through Q4 2026; site operating at ~50% capacity in the interim (c.£6m/month revenue, profit and cash drag), plus £25-30m of additional H2 exceptional costs expected

Q1 2026 AGM trading update: Group revenue up 11% at constant currency (Engines +20%, Airframes +4%); FY2026 guidance reiterated; no direct Middle East operating footprint, limited supply chain exposure to the Israel-Iran conflict

FY2025 results: revenue £3,589m (+8% LFL), adjusted operating profit £647m (+23%), margin up 240bps to 18.0%; first year of positive free cash flow (£125m), a key inflection point; full-year dividend raised 20% to 7.2p; new £175m buyback announced

Multiple commercial wins: Rolls-Royce sole-provider fan blade repair contracts, Pratt & Whitney GTF repair and additive (F135) development agreements, GE Industrial Gas Turbine additive order, Anduril/Project NYX UK MoD collaboration, BAE Systems Brontanax Collaborative Combat Aircraft programme, Archer Midnight airframe component supply expansion

items.notes: Excludes impact of Garden Grove incident; based on GBP/USD = 1.37 average exchange rate; implies Engines £1,700-1,800m and Airframes £2,050-2,150m
Excludes Garden Grove impact; implies c.19% margin at mid-point; Engines £565-595m, Airframes £170-190m, PLC costs c.£35m
Reflects ramp in OE deliveries for GTF, XWB and GEnx engines

items.metric: Free cash flow (after interest and tax)
items.notes: Excludes Garden Grove impact; factoring expected to add £30-50m net cash inflow included within this guidance; cash generation historically second-half weighted

items.target: c.£6m/month revenue, profit and cash reduction while at ~50% capacity; £25-30m additional exceptional costs in H2
items.notes: Full restart targeted 28 September 2026; total financial impact (including potential legal/regulatory costs beyond the $100m claims programme) not yet fully quantified
Driven by production ramp-up, growing RRSP aftermarket cash generation, and all 19 RRSP programmes turning cash positive in 2028 (GTF programmes specifically cash positive in 2028)
Versus FY2025 margin of 18.0% / H1 2026 18.5%; Engines targeted at mid-to-high 30s% margin with high single-digit revenue CAGR

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Peter Dilnot described H1 2026 as 'a good performance... building on the momentum from last year' and reiterated confidence in 'delivering sustained increases in profit and cash flow in the years ahead,' underpinned by record civil order backlogs and rising defence spending. Management stressed that, excluding Garden Grove, full-year guidance is unchanged, while flagging that the total financial impact of Garden Grove (including potential legal, regulatory and compensation costs beyond the $100m claims programme) remains uncertain and will be updated in due course.

bull_case: Record civil aircraft order backlogs (Airbus/Boeing backlogs stretching into the 2030s) combined with constrained OEM build rates support years of visible OE and aftermarket growth

RRSP aftermarket portfolio provides long-duration, high-margin, annuity-like cash flow (Engines margin already 33-34%) with further upside as newer engines (GTF, GEnx, XWB) mature and all 19 RRSPs turn cash positive by 2028

Structural increase in global defence spending (NATO's path to 3.5% of GDP, European rearmament, rising US budgets) provides a multi-year tailwind to the ~30% of revenue derived from defence, with upside optionality from uncrewed/autonomous vehicle programmes
Credible medium-term targets (c.£5bn revenue, 24%+ margin, £600m FCF, >20% EPS CAGR by 2029) with FY2025 having delivered the first year of positive free cash flow, an important de-risking milestone

Garden Grove outcome has de-risked relative to worst case - no criminal charges filed, financial impact capped via a defined $100m claims programme, and a clear restart timeline (28 September 2026) with FY2026 guidance otherwise unchanged
bear_case: Garden Grove incident carries unresolved tail risk - ongoing federal/state investigations, more than 30 civil lawsuits, potential civil enforcement penalties and an unquantified total financial impact beyond the $100m claims programme and H2 exceptional costs

High customer/programme concentration with a small number of OEMs (Airbus, Boeing, Pratt & Whitney, GE, Rolls-Royce); loss of content or a programme delay on any major platform would be difficult to offset
Persistent industry-wide supply chain constraints (forgings, castings, rare-earth powders) could continue to cap the pace at which OE ramp-up and margin expansion materialise
Airframes division structurally lower-margin (6-8%) than Engines and has required a multi-year transformation programme to reach current profitability, with inventory levels still elevated

Elevated net debt (£1,530m, 1.8x leverage) and reliance on non-recourse factoring (£387m) leave less balance sheet flexibility, and the share buyback has already been paused once in response to an unexpected event
